_provenance: SP-1 R0 E5 Nirmal J(t) perf gate. TWO measurements on gpubox (WSL2, 2x NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada 48GB sm_89, driver 13.2, Warp 1.14 / CUDA Toolkit 12.9, .venv/bin/python; nvmath-python[cu12] 0.9.0). Driver: benchmarks/xdd/e5_perf_nirmal.py (level 8 = 257x257 = 66049 nodes = 330245 DOFs, DOF-matched proxy for the 513x129=66177-node Nirmal mesh; marchable regime lam2=1e-1, Eg_hat=4, symmetric mu, 10 GHz rect-sin, dt=5ps, cuda:0). GPU run REQUIRES LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/wsl/lib (WSL libcuda shadowing). 'history' = pre-fix host-splu run (E-b, 2026-07-18). 'measured'/'gate' = the E5 FIX: XDDSystem(linsolver='cudss') wiring cuDSS (GPU sparse direct LU via nvmath) into the Newton solve (2026-07-18). Perf numbers are LEDGER-LOCKED, not CI-reasserted (test asserts the file parses + the recorded speedup matches the recorded arithmetic).

history._note: PRE-FIX host-splu measurement (E-b, kept for provenance). The GPU was IDLE during the solve (0% util, 642 MiB) — host scipy splu was the bottleneck. This is what the cuDSS fix replaced.
history.solver: host scipy splu (nonsymmetric sparse LU); Warp assembles element matrices on cuda:0 but the global Jacobian CSR is built on HOST and factorized on HOST. cuDSS NOT wired. Closures host numpy.
history.verdict: MISS (off by ~18-55x). Host-splu bound, GPU 0% util. This is the bottleneck the cuDSS fix addresses.

measured._size_note: 513x129 = 66177 nodes; no anisotropic octree in-tree (build_uniform is square 2^level). Measured at level 8 = 257x257 = 66049 nodes = 0.19% DOF match. Per-step cost is DOF/sparsity-governed (nondim h_hat in [0,1]), so the square proxy is faithful for perf.
measured.regime: marchable (lam2=1e-1, Eg_hat=4, symmetric mu=0.5). Physical PM6 config hits the documented CPU-mesh drive wall (Eg_hat~42.5, Debye<<h) -> Newton bails at iter 1 (unrepresentative). Marchable runs full Newton; LU size/sparsity (the dominant cost) is IDENTICAL to physical.
measured._step_walls_note: 8 timed steps; alternating 1-iter (~6.7-7.8s) and 3-iter (~21s) Newton solves -> ~7s per Newton iteration (vs ~96s/iter host splu). All 8 converged (cuDSS handles the plain nonsymmetric 5-field Jacobian cleanly).
measured._warmup_note: First step incl. Warp JIT compile + 4 Newton iters + cuDSS plan+factorize; one-time, excluded from s/step. Was 411s under host splu -> 12.6x faster warm-up.
measured._steps_note: 1 ns window at 5 ps/step = 200 steps + 1 (10 GHz -> 10 optical cycles, 20 steps/cycle).
measured.solver: cudss GPU sparse direct LU (nvmath-python DirectSolver, plain DirectSolverOptions(blocking=True) — no mtlayer_gomp; plan-once + reset_operands+refactorize per Newton iterate on the fixed sparsity; explicit .free() on pattern change/failure). Warp assembles element matrices on cuda:0; the global Jacobian CSR is still built on HOST and the A3 closures are HOST numpy.
measured._gpu_util_note: Bursty: 40-sample burst during the timed march caught 1x 100%, 3x 41%, 36x 0%. Peak 100% during the cuDSS factorize; 0% between solves because the per-step cost is now HOST-bound (Jacobian assembly + closures) — the GPU LU is fast enough to no longer be the bottleneck. Contrast: host-splu was a flat 0% (GPU never used for the solve).
measured._bottleneck: SHIFTED off the GPU LU. cProfile of one representative step (2 steps / 8 Newton iters, 33.1s): _reduce_and_eliminate host Jacobian assembly 12.4s/37% (scipy tolil 8.4s + lil.__init__ 2.05s); jacobian_full host element/closure build 10.5s/32% (einsum 4.2s + numpy tolist 4.17s + _supg/_mass blocks); _cudss_linsolve 5.96s/18% (of which cuDSS plan 4.7s is a one-time re-plan cost in this profile; steady-state _execute factorize+solve is the recurring GPU cost). => The NEXT bottleneck is HOST-side Jacobian assembly + closures (~69%), not the GPU solve. To reach >=100x: move the CSR assembly + A3 closures onto the device (the B4/B5 device-assembly path) and eliminate the host tolil/tolist hotspots.

gate._baseline_note: Nirmal paper CPU baseline: 10-30 h on 36 CPU cores for one J(t) trace.
gate._end_to_end_note: PROJECTION (labeled, honest): s_per_step_median x steps_for_window. Full 1 ns trace NOT run to completion; 8 timed steps + warm-up sufficient to lock the s/step (invariant to trace length).
gate.verdict: MISS vs 100x, but a REAL ~7x median (11.5x mean) speedup over the host-splu baseline (97.75 -> 14.12 s/step; 5.46 -> 0.79 h end-to-end). cuDSS moved the LU onto the GPU and off the critical path (per-Newton-iter ~96s -> ~7s, ~13x). The gate still misses because the bottleneck SHIFTED to HOST-side Jacobian assembly + closures (~69% of the step; GPU now idle between bursty solves, peaking 100% during factorize). Honest verdict: the cuDSS wiring is the correct, measured first step; the remaining ~8-14x to 100x requires moving the host assembly/closures onto the device (recorded as the next bottleneck).
gate._speedup_vs_history_note: cuDSS s/step 14.121 vs host-splu 97.752 = 6.92x median (160.47/14.01 = 11.45x mean; 95.18/6.66 = 14.3x on the 1-iter min). end-to-end 19648.2/2838.4 = 6.92x.
